identity.name: FiftySix Self-Winding
identity.one_liner: Vacheron's entry point — a steel 40mm round watch quoting the 1956 ref. 6073, with Maltese-cross lugs.

narrative.story: FiftySix launched at SIHH 2018 as Vacheron's play for a younger buyer, styled after the 1956 reference 6073 — each lug is a quarter of a Maltese cross. The steel 4600E was the cheapest way into the maison in decades, which cut both ways: the caliber 1326 base is shared architecture rather than a Geneva Seal in-house movement, and purists said so loudly. As a wearing proposition — 40mm, sector-ish dial, casual register — it holds up better than the forum verdict.
narrative.collector_notes: No Geneva Seal on the steel self-winding is the known compromise; the complete calendar and higher FiftySix models carry hallmarked in-house calibers. Steel examples depreciated meaningfully from retail, making the pre-owned 4600E one of the cheapest tickets into any of the big three maisons.
